value.body: A six-year Doctor of Pharmacy degree focused on clinical pharmacy: five years of study, with hospital postings in the later years, then a one-year internship or residency. Graduates may use the prefix "Dr." under PCI's Pharm.D regulations. It is regulated by the Pharmacy Council of India (PCI).

items.label: Course length
items.note: 5 years of study + 1-year internship or residency; B.Pharm holders can join a 3-year Post-Baccalaureate route

items.label: Intake per college
items.note: 10 seats for Pharm.D (Post-Baccalaureate); PCI can revise this
items.source: PCI Pharm.D Regulations 2008, as reproduced by universities

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Class 12 with Physics and Chemistry plus Mathematics or Biology, or a D.Pharm. Admission is through state entrance tests such as TS EAPCET and AP EAPCET, university tests, or Class 12 merit, depending on the state.

value.title: At a glance
items: Registration with a State Pharmacy Council is needed to work as a pharmacist.
Enrolment rose from ~37,800 in 2021-22 to ~43,500 in 2023-24.
Work spans hospital clinical pharmacy, clinical research, pharmacovigilance and drug information.
